items.title: Define the normative Evidence Environment architecture and ownership boundary
items.context: Establish one source of truth for execution, observation, receipt normalization, admissibility, and gate ownership without creating parallel evidence storage or lifecycle gates.
items.userSees: User sees the architecture rule "Agent proposes, Environment observes, Proof Admissibility evaluates, Gate decides" and an explicit current-versus-target support matrix.

happy.desc: Inspect the normative architecture and executable ownership registry -> execution, observation, receipt normalization, Proof Admissibility, Evidence Platform storage, and Task/Story/Release Gate decisions each have exactly one named owner that maps to the existing architecture; WHY: prevents a second evidence or lifecycle control plane.

Trace one accepted Environment observation from adapter boundary through the existing evidence surface to a Gate consumer -> the trace uses the shared evidence store and existing lifecycle decision path with no adapter-owned Done state; WHY: proves the abstraction is integrated rather than merely documented.

edge.desc: Load legacy evidence that predates Environment Descriptor metadata -> backward-compatible parsing remains available but absent identities are not synthesized into stronger admissibility; WHY: preserves compatibility without laundering weak provenance.

Register two environment kinds with different execution models -> both share the normative receipt boundary while domain-specific truth rules remain in their packs/policies; WHY: tests host-neutral ownership without collapsing domain semantics.

adversarial.desc: Provide an adapter result that asserts pass, Done, or release approval directly -> the architecture and runtime path reject or ignore that authority and require the existing Gate decision; WHY: enforces authority separation.

Search implementation and documentation for a parallel Evidence Environment store, independent admissibility engine, or duplicate Task/Story/Release Gate -> no competing owner is introduced; WHY: prevents architectural split-brain.

items.title: Implement the generic Environment Descriptor, Invocation Request, and Receipt contracts
items.context: Extend the existing claim-admissibility/evidence architecture with host-neutral typed identities, execution boundaries, reproducibility and trust metadata while preserving backward compatibility.
items.userSees: User sees registry validation report "default environment descriptor registry: PASS" and deterministic normalized envelope digests.

happy.desc: Create a supported-version Environment Descriptor, Invocation Request, and Receipt with subject, environment, invocation, command/executable, policy, and provenance identities -> schema validation succeeds and canonical normalization is byte-stable across repeated runs; WHY: proves the generic contract is identity-bound and reproducible.

Serialize then deserialize a valid contract envelope -> all security, isolation, reproducibility, trust, temporal, and epistemic-scope fields retain their meaning and the normalized digest is unchanged; WHY: guards evidence portability across hosts.

edge.desc: Validate the minimum supported descriptor/request/receipt and a maximal envelope with permitted optional metadata and reordered object keys -> both normalize deterministically without inventing omitted trust claims; WHY: covers schema boundaries and canonicalization.
Submit an unknown major contract version or unsupported environment kind -> validation fails closed with a structured reason and produces no admissible receipt; WHY: prevents silent semantic drift.

adversarial.desc: Alter subject, invocation, environment, executable, shell mode, policy identity, or receipt payload after binding -> validation detects every mismatch and rejects admissibility; WHY: prevents replay and identity substitution.

Inject unrecognized fields that claim elevated trust, independence, reproducibility, or gate authority -> normalization cannot upgrade the epistemic scope and validation fails or confines the fields as specified; WHY: blocks privilege escalation through extensibility.

items.title: Provide executable and receipt-reading reference adapter paths
items.context: Demonstrate that one contract covers a policy-authorized local-command reference path and the existing Quantum read-receipt-only scientific path. The local path must reuse the existing configured validation executor and must not expose a new arbitrary-command endpoint; actual cwd/path, argv/shell, effective process environment, executable identity, secrets/redaction, network, timeout/cancellation, output bounds, and Evidence Platform storage behavior fail closed under project policy.
items.userSees: User sees "code-runtime execute-local: PASS" and "quantum read-receipt-only: PASS" without any new arbitrary command endpoint.

happy.desc: Invoke an allow-listed local validation command through the existing configured executor -> bounded stdout/stderr and exit facts become a normalized Environment receipt stored through the Evidence Platform, with actual cwd, argv/shell mode, effective environment policy, executable identity, timeout, and network posture bound; WHY: proves a safe executable reference path without a new arbitrary runner.

Read a valid existing Quantum scientific receipt through the receipt-only adapter -> it normalizes to the same generic contract while preserving Quantum-specific claim scope and without executing a solver; WHY: demonstrates one boundary across executable and external-observation environments.

edge.desc: Run an allowed command that reaches timeout, cancellation, non-zero exit, or output limit -> the receipt records the bounded terminal observation deterministically and never converts it to a pass claim; WHY: covers failure timing and resource limits.

Read a validly shaped Quantum receipt whose source identity, freshness window, or required artifact is absent -> receipt parsing may diagnose it but Proof Admissibility remains fail-closed; WHY: separates normalization from acceptance.

adversarial.desc: Attempt command injection, shell-mode substitution, cwd/path escape, executable replacement, forbidden network access, or undeclared environment/secret access -> execution is refused before launch and no admissible success receipt is emitted; WHY: tests the local adapter security boundary.

Call the adapter with an arbitrary command not present in configured validation policy or search public handlers for a generic command endpoint -> invocation is rejected and no such endpoint exists; WHY: prevents the adapter contract becoming remote code execution.

items.title: Add fail-closed environment adapter conformance tests
items.context: Mechanically prove descriptor and receipt conformance, deterministic normalization, admissibility-level host substitution, and fail-closed rejection for unknown versions, subject/invocation/environment/executable/shell mismatch, stale or unsafe receipts, checker errors, forbidden execution, secret/network/path policy violations, forged producer identity, quorum substitution, and direct completion authority. Gate-level host substitution is rerun only after M5 integration.
items.userSees: User runs "npm --prefix packages/main run test:evidence-environment-adapter" and sees "evidence environment adapter smoke passed" after all tamper cases fail closed.

happy.desc: Run the Environment Adapter conformance suite against the local-command and Quantum receipt paths -> both pass descriptor, invocation, receipt, deterministic-normalization, authority-separation, and admissibility-scope checks; WHY: makes cross-environment compatibility mechanical.

Evaluate semantically equivalent fresh receipts produced through two host brands under the same subject, invocation, environment semantics, policy, and allowed trust class -> Proof Admissibility and the integrated Gate return the same decision; WHY: proves host-substitution invariance at both admissibility and Gate levels.

edge.desc: Exercise unknown versions, stale receipts, unsafe isolation metadata, checker exceptions, cancellation races, and malformed bounded output -> each case yields a deterministic structured failure and no admissible pass; WHY: verifies fail-closed behavior at operational boundaries.

Run canonicalization under reordered keys, equivalent path spelling allowed by policy, and repeated evaluation -> equivalent inputs produce the same digest while materially different executable or shell semantics do not collide; WHY: tests normalization precision.

adversarial.desc: Submit forged producer identity, replayed invocation binding, or two quorum inputs from the same producer lineage -> conformance and Gate checks reject the evidence as non-independent; WHY: prevents provenance forgery and quorum substitution.

Use a conformant adapter to assert completion, weaken a required Task/Story/Release check, or turn a checker error into success -> the attempt fails and existing lifecycle requirements remain authoritative; WHY: proves conformance does not confer completion power.

items.title: Publish the paper-facing abstraction and calibrated support claims
items.context: Publish the versioned paper-ready architecture section and claim-to-evidence support matrix in docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-evidence-environment-adapter-execution-plan.md, with an explicit external-manuscript handoff requirement and implementation commit/release binding. Wording may advance from Level A to B/C only after CHK-003/004 conformance and M5 Gate evidence; Lean, biology, PINN solver, deployment, and other unimplemented integrations remain future targets.
items.userSees: User sees "Implemented now: generic EEA contract, code-runtime execute-local receipt adapter, Quantum read-receipt-only adapter, conformance suite, and Proof Admissibility/Gate projection. Integration targets: Lean, Rosetta, AlphaFold, PINN solvers, browsers, databases, CI, Kubernetes, and production deployment."

happy.desc: Validate the paper-facing architecture section and claim-to-evidence matrix -> each stated contribution is labeled by support level, linked to a concrete implementation/conformance/Gate artifact, and bound to an implementation commit or release; WHY: makes publication claims auditable.

Follow the manuscript handoff instructions from the versioned decision document -> an external paper editor can distinguish the generic contract, implemented reference paths, Gate integration, and future targets without consulting hidden story state; WHY: ensures the deliverable is usable beyond the repository workflow.

edge.desc: Review claims for Lean, Rosetta, AlphaFold, PINN solvers, browsers, databases, CI, Kubernetes, and production deployment -> unimplemented integrations are consistently marked as targets/examples rather than current adapters; WHY: prevents scope inflation at the implementation boundary.

Evaluate the document before and after conformance/Gate evidence is available -> support wording advances only to the level justified by bound evidence and otherwise remains at the lower level; WHY: enforces evidence-dependent claim calibration.

adversarial.desc: Scan public-facing prose for assertions that Proof-or-Stop currently supports arbitrary environments or completed scientific/deployment adapters -> prohibited overclaims are absent or explicitly qualified; WHY: resists paper-language laundering.

Remove or stale the referenced implementation commit, release binding, conformance result, or M5 Gate evidence -> the support matrix can no longer report the associated higher claim level; WHY: prevents detached documentation from serving as proof.

items.title: Integrate Evidence Environment receipts with Proof Admissibility and lifecycle Gate consumers
items.context: Implement M5 as an explicit owner: normalized EEA receipts enter the shared proof-surface and Proof Admissibility path, diagnostic-only adapters remain non-gating, approved policies may strengthen but never weaken Task/Story/Release requirements, and Gate-level host substitution is verified with fresh evidence while forged or same-producer quorum inputs fail closed.
items.userSees: User sees Gate projection "admissible: advance" only for a fresh trusted receipt, while stale, forged, same-key quorum, or diagnostic-only evidence reports "stop".

happy.desc: Register a normalized fresh Environment receipt under an approved policy and evaluate its declared claim -> the shared proof surface and Proof Admissibility consume it, then the existing Task/Story/Release Gate consumer applies its own required checks; WHY: proves actual lifecycle integration without adapter-owned decisions.

Configure an approved domain policy that adds stronger evidence requirements -> the Gate enforces the added requirements while retaining every baseline lifecycle requirement; WHY: proves policies may strengthen but never weaken Proof-or-Stop.

edge.desc: Submit a diagnostic-only adapter receipt and a backward-compatible legacy receipt -> both remain observable, but neither gains gating force beyond explicitly admitted scope; WHY: preserves diagnostics and compatibility without accidental authority.

Replace the host brand while keeping subject, invocation, environment semantics, policy, freshness, provenance class, and normalized evidence equivalent -> the Gate decision is unchanged; changing an allowed trust or independence fact may change admissibility with an explicit reason; WHY: precisely bounds host-substitution invariance.

adversarial.desc: Submit a forged producer, stale/replayed binding, or same-producer evidence as independent quorum inputs -> Proof Admissibility and lifecycle Gate consumers fail closed and record the rejection reason; WHY: prevents fabricated independence from completing a lifecycle objective.

Attempt to use an adapter receipt to bypass a missing Task, Story, or Release requirement, downgrade a mandatory check, or write Done directly -> completion remains blocked and no adapter API has direct completion authority; WHY: protects the monotonic Gate invariant.
